title: chore: normalize line endings — `* text=auto eol=lf` + renormalize the 16 CRLF-committed files in one commit
description:
Why: the shared checkout is used by both Git for Windows (system core.autocrlf=true) and WSL git. Before the repo-local core.autocrlf=false pin of 2026-10-24, landings committed whole-file LF→CRLF flips. 15 source files are now stored as CRLF ("i/crlf"), plus moe-jetbrains/gradlew.bat, which was committed CRLF despite `text eol=crlf`. Raw diff stats run to thousands of lines (QA's >400-LOC check must use --ignore-cr-at-eol until this lands), and blame is polluted. Found and measured by qa-b0c1741e (msgs 17f13542, 33b5a4b4 in #governors).

Flipping commits (raw vs --ignore-cr-at-eol):
- 204d5a6 CQ-M01a: packages/moe-daemon/src/types/schema.ts, src/state/validators.ts, src/state/validators.test.ts
- f6a79ef CQ-F02: src/state/taskStore.ts, src/tools/submitPlan.test.ts
- 803a38d CQ-M01c: src/server/WebSocketServer.ts
- 9879f51 CQ-R02p: .github/workflows/ci.yml, moe-jetbrains/build.gradle.kts, moe-vscode/scripts/bundle-assets.mjs, scripts/tests/onboarding.mjs
- 1bb42e1 + db3172e CQ-M02: scripts/usage-receipt.mjs, scripts/usage-report.mjs, scripts/usage-session.mjs, scripts/tests/usage-receipt.test.mjs, scripts/tests/usage-report.test.mjs
- plus moe-jetbrains/gradlew.bat (pre-existing).

Do, in ONE dedicated commit:
(a) Make `* text=auto eol=lf` the first line of .gitattributes. The existing *.sh, gradlew, gradlew.bat and *.jar rules stay after it and keep overriding it.
(b) `git add --renormalize` exactly the 16 paths above, with no content edits.

(a) and (b) must land together. With (a) alone, the wrapper's moe_temp_index_build would again drop edits to any CRLF blob still in the index as MOE_ATTR_CONCURRENT: `git add` keeps it, while `hash-object` normalizes it. See the sibling hardening task.

Afterwards, hashing follows .gitattributes on Windows and WSL alike, checkouts write LF on both sides, and the ~195 .moe records still CRLF on disk read clean.

Sequencing: depends on CQ-M01 (task-ad95cb27), which carries CQ-M01d's stranded schema.ts doc-comment hunk as a declared file. Landing this first would sweep that hunk in. Also serialize against any in-flight task that holds one of the 16 paths (schema.ts, taskStore.ts and WebSocketServer.ts are hot in CQ). Leave the repo-local core.autocrlf=false in place; the attribute governs.
definitionOfDone: .gitattributes starts with `* text=auto eol=lf`; every pre-existing rule is unchanged and still follows it.
`git ls-files --eol | grep '^i/crlf'` prints nothing (all 16 listed paths renormalized), and moe-jetbrains/gradlew.bat is still checked out CRLF per its eol=crlf rule.
In the commit, `git diff --ignore-cr-at-eol --stat <parent>..<commit>` shows only .gitattributes: no content change to any of the 16 files.
Daemon tests (npm test), bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh, scripts/tests/postflight.ps1 and the parity checks all pass on the result, and moe-agent.ps1 keeps its UTF-8 BOM.
taskRails: Exactly one dedicated commit: the .gitattributes line plus renormalization of the 16 listed paths. No content edits and no other files.
Never hand-edit or normalize .moe/** records; daemon rewrites handle them.

implementationPlan.description:
Pre-flight gate. READ-ONLY: no file edits and no Git writes (only the wrapper lands). Any live-tree change before step 3 could be swept into a checkpoint commit and break the one-dedicated-commit rail.
The 16 paths (named in every step; affectedFiles lists only .gitattributes because the plan-size gate rejects more than 10 distinct files and the task rail forbids splitting - step 3 attributes the 16 with moe.declare_files): .github/workflows/ci.yml, moe-jetbrains/build.gradle.kts, moe-jetbrains/gradlew.bat, moe-vscode/scripts/bundle-assets.mjs, packages/moe-daemon/src/server/WebSocketServer.ts, packages/moe-daemon/src/state/taskStore.ts, packages/moe-daemon/src/state/validators.test.ts, packages/moe-daemon/src/state/validators.ts, packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/submitPlan.test.ts, packages/moe-daemon/src/types/schema.ts, scripts/tests/onboarding.mjs, scripts/tests/usage-receipt.test.mjs, scripts/tests/usage-report.test.mjs, scripts/usage-receipt.mjs, scripts/usage-report.mjs, scripts/usage-session.mjs.
All checks must pass, else stop:
(a) `git ls-files --eol | grep '^i/crlf'` lists a subset of the 16 (a path that is already LF in HEAD is skipped and named in the summary). Any CRLF path outside the 16 -> moe.report_blocked with the list and needsFrom 'architect' (the rail fixes the set).
(b) `git status --porcelain -- .gitattributes <the 16>` shows nothing except moe-jetbrains/gradlew.bat, and `git diff --ignore-cr-at-eol --quiet -- moe-jetbrains/gradlew.bat` exits 0 (its known EOL-only dirt: a CRLF blob under its own `text eol=crlf` rule). Any other dirt is someone's uncommitted work -> report_blocked naming the owner from (c).
(c) `moe.get_commit_scope { taskId, phase: 'postflight' }`: for every peerDeclared entry on .gitattributes or one of the 16, look up that task. If it has an assigned seat (in flight), OR your CLI has no Edit/Write tool (codex/gemini/grok seats have an always-empty TOOL tier, and a contested path lands only with a TOOL witness), call `moe.report_blocked { blockedOnTaskIds: [those ids], reason }` and end the session; it auto-clears when they reach DONE. A peer without an assigned seat is fine for a Claude seat: step 3 gives those paths TOOL witnesses.
Known holders are already wired as dependsOn: CQ-M01 (done), CQ-F03 task-bf86954d (schema.ts, taskStore.ts, validators.ts) and CQ-M04c task-e4adf15c (usage-report.test.mjs).
Error handling: any git or tool error here is a stop, never a guess.

Verification gate on a SNAPSHOT of the result. Still no live-tree edits. Build it: `SNAP=$(mktemp -d /tmp/moe-eol-gate.XXXXXX); git archive HEAD | tar -x -C $SNAP`. In $SNAP, prepend the line `* text=auto eol=lf` to .gitattributes and convert the 15 text=auto paths (the 16 minus moe-jetbrains/gradlew.bat, which stays CRLF on disk) with step 3's byte-level converter (replace b'\r\n' with b'\n', nothing else). Then run each suite and record its command, exit code and output tail:
1. `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test` is THE named verification command for complete_task. Run it from $SNAP/packages/moe-daemon with node_modules symlinked to the native Linux install (`ln -s /tmp/moe-linux-daemon.3EJTl5/repo/packages/moe-daemon/node_modules $SNAP/packages/moe-daemon/node_modules`; if that is gone, npm ci in a separate scratch copy with an unchanged lockfile), every MOE_* variable unset and a Linux-only PATH. The shared checkout's node_modules are Windows-native; never install there.
2. `bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh` from $SNAP (the harness root is its own directory; set MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC=180 on a busy box).
3. scripts/tests/postflight.ps1: copy $SNAP/scripts into a Windows-visible scratch dir (e.g. /mnt/d/moe-scratch/eol-<ts>/scripts) and run `powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File 'D:\moe-scratch\eol-<ts>\scripts\tests\postflight.ps1'` (Windows PowerShell 5.1 lives in /mnt/c/Windows/System32/WindowsPowerShell/v1.0/; pipe its output through `tr -d '\0'`). If no PowerShell can run it, say so plainly in the summary; never report a pass you did not run.
4. Parity: `bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh`, and scripts/tests/parity-check.ps1 through the same powershell.exe route.
5. Cheap extras on the converted scripts: `node --check` on each converted .mjs, and `node --test scripts/tests/usage-receipt.test.mjs scripts/tests/usage-report.test.mjs`.
6. BOM: `head -c3 scripts/moe-agent.ps1 | od -An -tx1` prints `ef bb bf`.
Run the long harnesses in the background, in parallel. If a suite fails, rerun it on a plain `git archive HEAD` snapshot: red there too means pre-existing (prove it and report it); red only on the result means stop and report_blocked with the evidence. Never edit tests or sources (rail: no content edits).

Apply to the live tree. Do this LAST and in one sitting, then go straight to step 4 and complete_task: the wrapper lands at session exit, so the window in which a peer's landing could sweep these bytes stays at minutes.
(a) .gitattributes: insert `* text=auto eol=lf` as the new first line with your editing tool. Every existing line stays byte-identical after it (`git diff -- .gitattributes` = exactly one added line at the top).
(b) Convert the 15 text=auto paths (the 16 minus gradlew.bat) with ONE deterministic script, e.g. `python3 -I`. For each path it reads `git cat-file blob HEAD:<path>` and the working file as bytes, and REFUSES (non-zero exit, nothing written) unless they are byte-identical, so no peer's bytes can ride in. It then writes `data.replace(b'\r\n', b'\n')` and reports any lone CR it kept. The result equals what `git add --renormalize` stores under the new attribute.
Do NOT run git add, --renormalize or any other Git write. With the CRLF blob still in the index, the wrapper's `git add` would keep CRLF (git's safer-autocrlf rule), and moe_temp_index_build's hash-object comparison would drop the path as MOE_ATTR_CONCURRENT. An LF working copy makes both sides agree.
(c) moe-jetbrains/gradlew.bat: no edit. It stays CRLF on disk, and its `text eol=crlf` rule makes the wrapper store an LF blob.
(d) TOOL witnesses: Claude seats only, and only for paths that step 1 found peer-declared by a task without a seat. After the conversion, Read the file's first lines, then do an Edit round trip (append a marker to line 1, then remove it). `sha256sum` before and after must match; on gradlew.bat this also proves CRLF survived.
(e) `moe.declare_files { taskId, paths: [.gitattributes plus every one of the 16 that changed], note }`. This is required for gradlew.bat, whose EOL-only dirt predates the session and is otherwise MOE_ATTR_PREEXISTING and never committed; it is harmless for the rest. Report the same paths in complete_step.modifiedFiles.

Adversarial self-review, read-only proofs, then complete_task immediately (load adversarial-self-review).
Proofs on the live tree, all read-only:
- `head -n1 .gitattributes` is exactly `* text=auto eol=lf`, and the rest is unchanged.
- `git ls-files --eol -- <15 paths>` shows `w/lf attr/text=auto eol=lf` (the i/ column stays crlf until the wrapper lands and refreshes the index); gradlew.bat shows `w/crlf attr/text eol=crlf`.
- `git diff --ignore-cr-at-eol --stat -- .gitattributes <the 16>` lists only .gitattributes (1 insertion).
- Each converted path `cmp`s equal to its CR-stripped HEAD blob. `git hash-object --stdin-paths` (read-only, no -w) over the 16 equals `git hash-object --stdin` of each CR-stripped HEAD blob, so the landing stores LF blobs with identical content.
- `moe.get_commit_scope { taskId, phase: 'postflight' }`: your asserted/declared paths are exactly the changed set, and nothing else of yours is dirty. Re-check peerDeclared against step 1.
Attack the result: could a peer byte ride in (cmp guard), a lone CR be lost, the BOM change, an extra path land, or a checkpoint have carried part of it (none should exist, since nothing was edited before step 3)? If anything changed after step 2, rerun step 2 first.
Then complete_task with verification = step 2's daemon command, exit 0 and its output tail. The summary lists every suite result and the proofs above, plus these QA notes:
(1) The completion commit also carries the wrapper's .moe BOARD records (commitBoardState). Check DoD 3 as `git diff --ignore-cr-at-eol --stat <sha>^ <sha> -- . ':(exclude).moe'` = only .gitattributes, plus `git diff --stat <sha>^ <sha> -- <the 16>` showing EOL-only rewrites.
(2) DoD 2's `git ls-files --eol | grep '^i/crlf'` depends on the wrapper's shared-index refresh. If the landing printed MOE_COMMIT_INDEX_REFRESH_FAILED, use `git cat-file blob <sha>:<path> | grep -c $'\r$'` = 0 for each path instead.

reopenReason: Feed rule (human-approved, by order): prerequisite CQ-M01 is already planned (WORKING). MEDIUM, so it is planned after HIGH CQ rows; execution waits for CQ-M01 to land.

comments.author: architect-6e3edf85
comments.content:
Architect notes for the worker and QA (planRevision 1).

1. **affectedFiles lists only .gitattributes, on purpose.** The honest file count is 17. submit_plan hard-rejects plans over 10 distinct files, and this task's rail forbids splitting the work. All 16 renormalized paths are named in every step. The worker attributes them with moe.declare_files, plus Edit round trips for any contested path.

2. **Why the working copies are converted to LF instead of running `git add --renormalize`.** Agents never write Git. The wrapper lands from a temp index seeded from HEAD, so a renormalized shared index would never reach the commit. With the CRLF blob still in that index, git keeps CRLF on add (safer-autocrlf) while hash-object normalizes to LF, and the wrapper would drop each path as MOE_ATTR_CONCURRENT. That is the sibling task-b62c9fc7 defect. A byte-level CRLF→LF working copy makes the landing store exactly the blobs that --renormalize would.

3. **Dependencies added.** I added dependsOn CQ-F03 (task-bf86954d: schema.ts, taskStore.ts, validators.ts) and CQ-M04c (task-e4adf15c: usage-report.test.mjs). Both are live holders of these paths.

4. **DoD 3 as written vs. the commit.** The completion commit will also carry the wrapper's .moe BOARD records (commitBoardState default). Check DoD 3 on the non-.moe paths: `git diff --ignore-cr-at-eol --stat <sha>^ <sha> -- . ':(exclude).moe'` should show only .gitattributes.

5. **DoD 2 depends on the shared-index refresh.** DoD 2's `git ls-files --eol` reads the shared index, which the wrapper refreshes after landing. If the landing printed MOE_COMMIT_INDEX_REFRESH_FAILED, verify each path with `git cat-file blob <sha>:<path> | grep -c $'\r$'` = 0.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- Worker runs `git add --renormalize`: rejected. Agents never write Git, and the wrapper lands from a temp index seeded from HEAD, so a renormalized shared index would never reach the commit anyway.
- .gitattributes edit alone: rejected. With CRLF blobs in the index, the wrapper's temp-index `git add` keeps CRLF (git's safer-autocrlf rule) while `hash-object` normalizes to LF, so moe_temp_index_build drops every path as MOE_ATTR_CONCURRENT (the sibling task-b62c9fc7 defect). Converting the working copies to LF first makes both agree, and the stored blobs equal what --renormalize stores.
- Splitting to respect the 10-file cap: rejected by the task rail (one dedicated commit). affectedFiles lists only .gitattributes. The 16 paths are named in every step and attributed by moe.declare_files, plus TOOL witnesses when contested.
- Running the suites on the live tree: rejected. Live edits would open a long window for checkpoints and peers' PLANNED-tier whole-file sweeps. The snapshot equals the result byte for byte, and the live apply happens last, right before complete_task.
- More attribute rules (e.g. for other Windows scripts): out of scope by rail. gradlew.bat is the only .bat in the repo, and its rule stays.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Census at plan time: 1184 i/lf, exactly the listed 16 i/crlf, 2 i/-text (binary).
- gradlew.bat shows `M` only because its CRLF blob violates its own `text eol=crlf` rule: the raw diff is 112/112 lines, the --ignore-cr-at-eol diff is empty.
- scripts/moe-agent.ps1 is i/lf and starts with a UTF-8 BOM (ef bb bf).
- Repo-local core.autocrlf=false.
Wrapper mechanics:
- moe_temp_index_build is at scripts/moe-agent.sh ~4021: read-tree HEAD into a temp index, `git add :(literal)p`, compare with the hash-object snapshot blob.
- index_refresh (~4110) runs `git reset -q -- <landed paths>` on the shared index, so `git ls-files --eol` shows i/lf after landing.
- Tiers: declare_files is committed regardless of baseline. Pre-existing untouched dirt is MOE_ATTR_PREEXISTING. A contested path needs a TOOL witness under attribution.contested=skip-untouched.
- get_commit_scope ignores the plan paths of peers that wait on this task.
- The completion commit also stages BOARD records.
planningNotes.risks:
- Peer sweep: an in-flight peer whose plan names one of the 16 would commit the converted file whole on its next exit. Mitigated by dependsOn (F03, M04c), the step-1 gate, and doing live edits last.
- Codex/gemini/grok seats cannot produce TOOL witnesses, so they block on any declaring peer instead of landing a partial set.
- DoD 3's literal --stat also lists the wrapper's .moe BOARD records. Read it as non-.moe paths; QA note in step 4.
- A failed shared-index refresh leaves `git ls-files --eol` stale. Use the cat-file CR count.
- Long harness runtimes; postflight.ps1 needs Windows PowerShell via WSL interop. Prove pre-existing failures on plain HEAD.
- After landing, checkouts on both sides write LF for every text file except the explicit eol=crlf rule. Expected and intended.
